label: copy phase: input b while outputting b (copying a bb pair), late positions
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the input token is b (the model just emitted b), and almost entirely when the current output is also b, i.e. while copying a doubled b (bb) from the original. It never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter. Strongest at the first b of a bb run (input b, output b); within bbb runs the second b->b step is weaker (about 0.4-0.6 of the first). It is weak or absent when the bb pair is near the start of the sequence (recall_idx <= 2). Residual low-magnitude activity (about 7% of mass) appears on input b with a different output, mostly s. Dev: P 0.95, R 0.74, F1 0.83, mass recall 0.89.

issues: Minor: recall is about 0.70. About 24% of active test steps are input b with an output other than b (precision 0.0065 for that class, 8.8% of activation mass). The largest piece is output s (precision 0.08-0.12, about 4% of mass). Sub-predicates on next_out==b, to_go==0, in_count==1 and recall_idx>=5 each have precision below 0.08, so this looks like scattered weak noise, not a systematic class. The explanation already discloses it.
Checked: the feature never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and 100% of activation mass is on input b (profile).

Checked: bb pairs at recall_idx==2 have precision 0.24 and 3.4% of mass on the test split. Dropping the recall_idx>=3 clause lowers dev F1 from 0.83 to 0.71. The 'weak or absent near the start' claim holds.

Checked: the second b->b step in bbb runs (prev_tok==b) has precision 0.79 but only 2.6% of mass, which matches 'weaker'. Activation there varies (one example is 0.19, below the stated 0.4-0.6 range).
Checked: false positives at the last step (to_go==0) are few; that slice has precision 0.92.
Reproduced the test scores: P 0.937, R 0.704, F1 0.804, mass recall 0.878 (prev_tok!=b variant: F1 0.79). Adding output s drops F1 to 0.63, so no better predicate was found.
